title: Chizkiya Turgemina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman writes: In Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot, no such Amora is found. Others have already taken issue with them: the Gaon, author of Erekh Milin, entry ‘Amora’, p. 121; R-Sh Buber of blessed memory in Otzar HaSifrut, vol. 4, p. 173; the Gaon, author of Nachal Eden; and in דו״ר, Dorot HaRishonim, vol. 3, p. 46, note 11; and in HaKerem; and in Otzar Yisrael. All of them prophesy in one style, based on what is mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah 65:11, which reads: ‘And he said to him (to Esau), “My son”; and he said, “Here I am” — this is what is written (Proverbs 27): “When he speaks graciously, do not trust him”; Hizkiyah Turgemina said (ibid.): “for there are seven abominations in his heart.”’

Hyman responds: With due respect to them, they all erred in what they saw. This is not the name of an Amora; rather, it refers to King Hezekiah, as is known: from chapter 25 in Proverbs they said, ‘These too are the proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah copied.’ This is what the Midrash means: ‘This is what is written, “When he speaks graciously, do not trust him”’ (and this is a parenthetical statement, that Hezekiah, who copied Solomon’s words, stated the reason because) ‘there are seven abominations in his heart.’ And this is clear.

notes.text: Hyman rejects the interpretation that Chizkiya Turgemina is an amora and proposes King Hezekiah instead. This is his interpretation. His supplied Proverbs27 locator for “When he speaks graciously” differs from the familiar26:25 location and still needs a matching named citation check.

The digital name חזקיהו תורגמינא differs from supplied חזקיה תורגמינא; the heading Chizkiya and existing body Hizkiyah are preserved without harmonizing names, expanding Turgemina into a role, or accepting an authority identity. The printed notice (volume II, p. 423, continuing between columns on the same page) confirms the supplied Proverbs chapter 27. The separately consulted Proverbs 26:25 contains both “when he speaks graciously, do not trust him” and the seven abominations; Proverbs 25:1 names the men of King Hezekiah copying Solomon’s proverbs. The whole consulted Bereshit Rabbah 65:11 likewise cites 26:25 and writes חזקיהו תורגמינא. These are named textual comparisons, not a correction to Hyman’s Hebrew or an independent identification of the Midrash’s speaker with the king. His assertion that the other scholars all erred, that this is not an Amora but the king, and that the conclusion is clear retains its full force as his argument. His claims about Yuchasin, Seder HaDorot and the named scholarly works have not been established by a new exhaustive survey or collation. The bibliographic abbreviations, heading/body spelling difference and existing notes remain unchanged.
